question.knowledge_point: Solving a Trigonometric Equation Containing a Transformed Tangent Function Under a Modified Domain
question.problem: Consider the equation $\operatorname{tan}⁡(2x+\frac{\pi }{3})=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}$ for $-\pi <x\le \pi .$ If the exact solutions ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},{x}_{3}$ and ${x}_{4}$ are written in ascending order, what is the value of ${x}_{2}+{x}_{3}?$
question.worked_solution:
We will find the general solution to the equation, and then generate all of the solutions in the required domain.

The general solution to our equation is

$$
\begin{aligned}2x+\frac{\pi }{3} & =\frac{\pi }{6}+n\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

Solving the equation above for $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}2x & =\frac{\pi }{6}-\frac{\pi }{3}+n\pi  \\ 2x & =-\frac{\pi }{6}+n\pi  \\ x & =-\frac{\pi }{12}+\frac{n\pi }{2} \\ x & =\frac{(6n-1)\pi }{12}.\end{aligned}
$$

We set $n=0,\pm 1,\pm 2,…,$ until we have generated all solutions in the domain $-\pi <x\le \pi .$

- Setting $n=-1$ gives $x=-\frac{7\pi }{12}$

- Setting $n=0$ gives $x=-\frac{\pi }{12}$

- Setting $n=1$ gives $x=\frac{5\pi }{12}$

- Setting $n=2$ gives $x=\frac{11\pi }{12}$

All other values of $n$ generate solutions outside the domain $-\pi <x\le \pi .$ So, the solutions ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},{x}_{3},{x}_{4}$ (written in ascending order) are

$$
x=-\frac{7\pi }{12},\,-\frac{\pi }{12},\,\frac{5\pi }{12},\,\frac{11\pi }{12}.
$$

Finally, since ${x}_{2}=-\frac{\pi }{12}$ and ${x}_{3}=\frac{5\pi }{12},$ we have

$$
{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}=-\frac{\pi }{12}+\frac{5\pi }{12}=\frac{\pi }{3}.
$$
